isolation_policy: bubblewrap mount namespace: only the workspace, the policy-accepted read allowlist and the opencode runtime exist; the repository, the other arms' results, the earlier sessions and the global opencode configuration (its MCP servers and plugins) are not mounted; plus the opencode v2 permission object (bash denied, edit and write denied, read and external_directory deny-by-default with the explicit allowlist)
limitations: The mount namespace is the filesystem guarantee; the model provider is reachable over the shared network, so a model that was shown a file can still send it away.
sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: CURV-RESID-CONTRAST
TITLE: Curved residual chain with a behaviour-contrast anisotropic metric: the RQ-VAE quantizes in a Poincaré ball so that the training-only successor-vs-matched-null contrast direction absorbs code capacity before the deeper tokens do
MOTIVATION: In RQ-VAE the SID is a residual chain: level-0 explains most of the item, and the later tokens only explain what level-0 left over. For a generative next-item recommender the later tokens must be predictable from the prefix, i.e. they should carry behaviour-predictable variation, not encoder noise. The measured evidence here says what predicts Recall@10 is a behaviour-contrast quantity (successor-vs-null distance contrast), not hierarchy and not curvature; here that contrast is made the thing the residual chain spends code on, inside a curved metric where the same tangent residual moves the codeword point by a state-dependent amount.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds put behaviour into the codebook update (successor-weighted Fréchet means), into per-level curvature (CURVCTRL, which the gauge evidence undermines), into radial ranking (BRad-RQ) or into prefix/subtree boosting. This idea never sets curvature from data, never uses a Fréchet mean, and never uses a radius rank: curvature is a declared gauge (c=1), and behaviour enters as an anisotropic direction plus a gain INSIDE the residual-chain assignment rule, multiplied by the conformal factor of the ball. The coupling lives in the quantizer's argmin and in the exponential-map composition, not in an auxiliary loss beside the quantizer.
CHANGE: Each level's codeword is chosen by minimizing a curved, contrast-weighted quadratic form of the transported residual (gain alpha_i along the behaviour direction u_i, uniform orthogonal), and the prefix point advances by an exponential map instead of a vector addition.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Map frozen item text embedding z_i to x_i = exp_0(s z_i) with c=1, s = 0.9/max_i||z_i||. Precompute once, from the training split only, alpha_i and unit u_i (see BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION). Quantize x_i by the greedy curved chain of SPEC EQUATIONS. Train the encoder and the codebooks with that same per-level objective plus the standard commitment term; the codebooks receive the gradient of the curved objective, so their positions are shaped by the curved metric rather than by a Euclidean mean.'}
COST: No extra epochs. One preprocessing pass: 24556 items x (32 successor draws + 32 null draws), two log maps each, O(n*d) memory (about 12-25 MB at d=64-128); minutes once, off the training clock. Per optimisation step at the frozen scale (global batch 4096, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs): L x K x 4096 closed-form ball distances (L=3, K=256 gives 3.1M), each O(d) plus one scalar conformal factor and one rank-1 transport correction; roughly 2-3x the baseline nearest-neighbour quantizer cost, which is a minor fraction of a step because the text/ID encoder dominates. Expected Stage2 wall-clock overhead 3-6 percent, Stage3 cost unchanged.
HYPOTHESIS: If the contrast direction computed from training transitions marks variation the generator can actually predict, then absorbing that direction earlier in the chain makes prefix-conditioned next-token prediction easier, and Stage3 test_recall@10 rises above 0.065 while the code-space within-successor / within-null distance ratio falls. Observed by per-level token-flip rate against the baseline SIDs (small at level 0, large at levels 1-2), the code-space contrast ratio, hyperbolic residual norms per level, and finally test_recall@10 from the single frozen Stage3 run.
RISKS: ['The contrast direction may be dominated by popularity even after null matching, drifting codes toward popular items; the curved chain may saturate near the boundary and raise reconstruction error; greedy per-level curves only bite from level 1 (level 0 sits at the origin); and better code-space contrast may not become token-level predictability, which is exactly what the one run must reveal.']
END IDEA

IDEA: GYROFRAME-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-pole gyroframe residual quantization: RQ codes are emitted, assigned and composed inside the moving Lorentz frame of each item's train-only successor-contrast direction, with the pole at a constant one-curvature-unit radius.
MOTIVATION: Content-only RQ-VAE SIDs group items by what they are, but a generative next-item recommender needs prefixes that already carry "what tends to follow this" information; the repository measurements show the predictor of Recall is a behaviour CONTRAST quantity, not hierarchy and not curvature magnitude, so the contrast has to enter the code assignment itself rather than decorate it. An item whose successor contrast points one way and an item whose successor contrast points another way should not receive the same level-1 token just because their text embeddings are close.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here changed the curvature per prefix level, ranked each item's radius by behaviour entropy, or replaced the codebook update with a curved Fréchet mean. This one keeps the curvature fixed at c=1 (the gauge is not estimated), keeps a single constant pole radius for every item (no behaviour statistic ranks items radially), and instead uses the behaviour contrast to choose the DIRECTION of a Lorentz frame change: the quantizer's residual is taken at a behaviour-defined base point and each code is parallel-transported into that base point's tangent space, so the item-specific gyration (a pure curvature effect with no Euclidean analogue at the same cost) is what mixes behaviour into the code indices.
CHANGE: The RQ target point is the item's content point, but the composition starts at a behaviour pole p_i = exp_o(1 * u_hat_i) instead of the origin, and every codebook vector is parallel-transported from T_o into T_{z_{l-1}} before it is compared with the residual; the encoder output is projected orthogonal to u_hat_i so the encoder cannot undo the behaviour shift.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Lorentz model, curvature c=1 fixed, signature (-,+,...,+), <x,x>_L = -1. Pole: u_i = sum_{j in succ(i)} A_ij t_j - (sum_j A_ij) t_pop, A_ij = max(0, log(N*n_ij/(n_i*n_j))) clipped at log N, t_pop = popularity-weighted mean text direction; u_hat_i = u_i/||u_i||, p_i = exp_o(u_hat_i) (geodesic radius exactly 1, Poincaré radius tanh(1)=0.762, below the measured saturation point). Encoder: a_i = f_phi(e_i) projected orthogonal to u_hat_i and clipped to ||a_i||<=1. Item point x_i = exp_o(a_i). Quantization: z_0 = p_i; for l=1..L, r_l = log_{z_{l-1}}(x_i), k_l = argmin_k || r_l - PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k}) ||^2, z_l = exp_{z_{l-1}}( PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k_l}) ). SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L). The decoder keeps the baseline content reconstruction from d_i = log_o(z_L). Loss = baseline reconstruction + sum_l [ ||r_l - c~_{l,k_l}||^2 + ||r_l - sg(c~)||^2 + beta ||sg(r_l) - c~||^2 ] with c~ = PT_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k}).'}
COST: Per step at the frozen scale (batch 4096, L=4, d=64): 9 closed-form Lorentz maps per item (5 log/exp for the residual-and-compose recursion, 4 transports, each O(d), no matrices) = about 18 kflops per item, about 74 MFLOP forward and about 0.2 GFLOP forward+backward per step; 24 steps per epoch gives about 5 GFLOP per epoch and about 16 TFLOP over 3000 epochs, i.e. well under 1 percent of a 4-GPU transformer step. One-off offline preprocessing: one pass over the training interactions to build n_ij, n_i, n_j (minutes on CPU), one N-by-d pole table (24556 by 64 float32 = 6.3 MB) held as a non-trainable buffer and gathered by item id, so no per-step graph and no extra parameter. Expected wall clock within 1 percent of the baseline 3000-epoch Stage 2 run.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping only if (a) the item-specific transport rotation is large enough to move code assignment (the mean gyration angle of PT_{o->p_i} on the orthogonal complement is of order the geodesic distance, i.e. O(1) rad at radius 1, recorded once at initialisation, and the level-1 code histogram differs from the Euclidean-shift variant by a large fraction of items), and (b) the resulting SIDs are more successor-predictive, observed as a drop in the train-only prefix successor entropy and, finally, as Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run. If instead the encoder drives the achievable SID set to a relabelling of the baseline's, the run lands at baseline recall and the idea is dead.
RISKS: ['The encoder still has second-order freedom to compensate the frame shift, so the coupling can be partially absorbed (diagnostic: record ||<a_i,u_hat_i>|| and the mean hyperbolic displacement ||log_{p_i}(x_i)|| per epoch). Items with noisy one-transition successor sets get a full-strength direction because the radius is constant, which may inject PMI noise into level-1 codes (no shrinkage by design, to stay out of the radial-ranking slot). The displacement target has norm up to 2 at radius 1, so the L-level budget is stretched and reconstruction can degrade, which would make SIDs less informative for Stage 3 even if they are more behaviour-aligned. Fixed-radius poles for rare items may also increase SID collisions where successor contrast is uninformative; collision count and distinct-SID count are recorded but are not gates.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BCGR-LORENTZ
TITLE: Behaviour-contrast geodesic re-anchoring of the RQ-VAE residual chain in the Lorentz model
MOTIVATION: Evidence in this repository says the useful SID metric family is behaviour *contrast*, and that its Euclidean control matches the hyperbolic form, while the radial coordinate is only group compactness and the four-point/tree premise is unavailable. That leaves one unexamined place for geometry to do real work: the quantization residual. In a Euclidean RQ chain the residual z - q mixes radial error (which the evidence says is uninformative) with directional error (which carries behaviour identity), so levels 2 and 3 spend their codebook capacity re-encoding radius. BCGR makes the residual an angular, behaviour-oriented quantity: it measures the correction from a point displaced along the item's train-only behavioural flow, in a chart where pure radius changes are cheap and direction changes are expensive.
NOVELTY: Prior mechanisms here changed the codebook update rule (successor-weighted Frechet means), the per-level curvature (CURVCTRL), or the item radius (BRad). BCGR changes none of those: the codebook, the number of levels and the loss terms are untouched. It changes *where the log map is taken from* - the residual anchor is displaced by a behaviour-contrast term - and it therefore changes what levels >= 2 are asked to encode (behaviour-orthogonal direction instead of radius). No cone, no prefix-transition score, no Gromov-delta weight, no radial ranking.
CHANGE: At every RQ level the residual is taken at a displaced anchor q~ = exp_q(delta_i * u_i) instead of at the codeword q, where delta_i is the item's train-only forward/backward transition asymmetry times the codeword's own hyperbolic radius and u_i is the parallel transport to q of the successor-centroid direction; the next-level input is the parallel transport of log_{q~}(z) back to the origin and every assignment uses the Lorentz distance.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Fix the gauge at curvature c = 1 (documented choice; re-scaling by sqrt(c) reproduces any other curvature exactly). Work on the hyperboloid H^d = {x in R^{d+1}: <x,x>_L = -1}, <u,v>_L = -u0 v0 + u.v, lift L(z) = (sqrt(1+||z||^2), z), d_H(x,y) = arcosh(clamp(-<x,y>_L, 1+1e-7, inf)).\nTrain-only statistics per item i: n_ij = number of times item j directly follows item i in training sessions; p_i(j) = n_ij / sum_j n_ij, p~_i(j) = n_ji / sum_j n_ji; alpha_i = 0.5 * sum_j |p_i(j) - p~_i(j)| in [0,1]; s_i = sum_j p_i(j) * e_j with e_j the frozen side/text embedding of item j; v_i = P s_i / max(||P s_i||, 1e-8) with P a learned d_in x d linear map; u_i = PT_{O->q}(v_i) with O = (1,0,...,0).\nPer level l with codeword q_l: delta_i = alpha_i * d_H(O, q_l) (automatically <= d_H(O,q_l), clipped at 0.5 * d_H(O,q_l) for safety); q~_l = exp_{q_l}(delta_i * u_i); residual tangent r_l = PT_{q~_l -> O}( log_{q~_l}( L(z_l) ) ); next input z_{l+1} = exp_O(r_l); assignment a_{l+1} = argmin_k d_H(L(z_{l+1}), q_{l+1,k}). Commitment term uses ||r_l||^2 in place of ||z_l - q_l||^2; reconstruction loss unchanged. alpha_i = 0 -> delta = 0 -> exact baseline anchor.'}
COST: One-time pass over training sessions to build sparse n_ij and s_i (O(#train transitions), minutes, CPU, cached). Per step nothing changes in the transformer; the added work is 4096 items x 3 levels x (one log, one exp, two parallel transports, ~4 d-dimensional ops) plus a 4096 x 3 x 257 Lorentz-dot assignment in R^(d+1), about 1.1e8 FLOPs forward per step against a transformer step of order 1e12, i.e. well under 1% per step. Per epoch at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps, 3000 epochs) the re-anchoring is ~1.2e9 FLOPs per epoch, no extra codebook entries and one extra d_in x d matrix; measured wall-clock expectation +1% to +2% on the four-card Stage 2 run, negligible on Stage 3 because Stage 3 consumes the emitted SIDs only.
HYPOTHESIS: If the radial coordinate is the uninformative part of the code space (evidence 3) and behaviour contrast is the informative part, then removing radius from the residual should make levels 2 and 3 encode behaviour-distinguishing direction, so the train-split conditional entropy H(next | 2-level prefix) and H(next | 3-level prefix) at fixed first token should fall relative to the frozen baseline, level-2/3 code usage should spread rather than concentrate on a few radial codes, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065 in the single frozen run. If the residual re-anchoring is neutral (delta too small to matter because most codewords sit near the origin) the diagnostics will show unchanged level-2 entropy and unchanged recall, which is the falsification.
RISKS: ['(1) Early in training P and the codebook are unaligned, so u_i points somewhere unhelpful and the displacement injects noise into levels 2-3; 3000 epochs may not be enough to recover. (2) If codewords cluster near the origin, d_H(O,q) ~ 0 and delta ~ 0, making the mechanism a no-op - this is detectable in the diagnostics but leaves the run uninformative. (3) Behaviour contrast may already be fully exploited by the level-1 assignment, so the residual change is redundant. (4) The learned P has a single gradient pathway and could collapse to a constant direction, in which case alpha only rescales a fixed displacement (harmless but weak).']
END IDEA

IDEA: GYROFRAME-RQ__ideation_4
TITLE: Behaviour-conditioned moving frame (Mobius gyro-translation by a positive-PMI transition direction) for the RQ-VAE residual recursion in a fixed-curvature Poincare ball
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built by subtracting codebook vectors from a residual, so every deeper level re-encodes the item's absolute position rather than what distinguishes it from the items it is actually confused with at recommendation time. The repository evidence shows that what predicts Stage3 recall is behaviour contrast (HBAA +0.7104) and not hierarchy, curvature estimation or radial compactness, yet the quantizer recursion has no notion of where an item's behaviour is heading; its levels 2..L are spent on global geometry instead of behaviour-relevant deviation.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (Poincare-Frechet successor centroids), the per-level curvature (CURVCTRL-SID), the radial slot (BRad-RQ), the prefix cone (behcone-prefix-rq), successor profile smoothing (LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ), successor boosting (succboost-geoshift), MoE branching (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ) and multi-curvature fibres (MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ). None of them touches the residual recursion operator itself. GYROFRAME-RQ changes p_{l+1} from "p_l minus code" to "p_l minus code, re-expressed in a per-item frame that is gyro-translated by the item's behaviour contrast direction". The displacement is directional only (constant hyperbolic radius), so it is not a radial or depth ranking, and curvature is never estimated (fixed c=1, explicitly a gauge choice).
CHANGE: At each level the residual point is moved into the item's behaviour frame by the Poincare isometry tau_{m_i}, the chosen code is subtracted there by Mobius addition, and the result is logged back to the tangent space to become the next residual, so the codes chosen at levels 2..L are determined jointly by the behaviour direction and by the curved frame change.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'k_l = argmin_k d_P(E_sigma(r_l), E_sigma(e_k)); p_{l+1} = (-E_sigma(e_{k_l})) (+) ((-m_i) (+) E_sigma(r_l)); r_{l+1} = L_sigma(p_{l+1}); m_i = tanh(rho) u_i, where u_i is the positive-PMI transition contrast direction and rho, sigma are measured once and frozen. Full equations under SPEC EQUATIONS.'}
COST: Precompute once, offline, before training: the sparse train-transition PMI weights plus one sparse-times-dense product (~10^6 edges x 768 dims ~ 0.8 GFLOP), and the 24556 x 768 anchor table (75 MB float32); a few seconds to one minute, zero per-step cost afterwards. Per training step (global batch 4096, L levels, d = 768): L x 4096 x 768 x ~10 flops ~ 1.3e8 FLOPs = 0.13 GFLOP plus ~4 extra 4096 x 768 activations (~55 MB); that is under 1-2% of a transformer step. At the frozen scale 24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, total extra ~9.4 TFLOP, wall-clock overhead about 1%. No new trainable parameters; the anchor table is a non-trainable buffer.
HYPOTHESIS: For the idea to be worth keeping, the behaviour frame must move deep-level capacity away from global position and toward transition-relevant deviation, so that a 3-token prefix becomes more predictive of the training successor set and the frozen Stage3 beam puts the true item in the top 10 more often than 0.065. Observable: at the final checkpoint, evaluating the same weights with m_i forced to 0 (forward pass only, no retraining) must change a large fraction of level>=2 codes and worsen the train-split prefix successor rank; if the both-on run's Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 while the geometry-off switch on the same checkpoint yields different level>=2 codes, the coupling is doing work.
RISKS: ['The frame offset may be noise for items whose PMI direction is dominated by popularity artefacts (reduced but not removed by the PMI normalisation). The discrete argmin passes gradient to the curved chain only through the straight-through cost, so the codebook may adapt weakly and the frame may act as a fixed perturbation. If latents crowd the ball boundary, artanh saturation makes the frame change enormous. The constant-radius anchor may be too weak or may dominate. Stage3 may simply ignore the changed tokens, in which case one run cannot tell which sub-part failed.']
END IDEA

IDEA: CONFORMAL-SUCC-RQ
TITLE: A behaviour-conditioned conformal factor deforms the Lorentz-chart distance used by the RQ-VAE residual assignment, so successor-concentrated items get finer code resolution.
MOTIVATION: The evidence says SID quality is predicted by behaviour contrast, not by hierarchy: HBAA-style distance contrast tracks recall (+0.71) while Gromov-delta and ancestor-depth weighting hurt. Degree-matched rewiring is as tree-like as the real graph, so "the data is a tree" is unavailable. What is still unused is the graph's own local concentration: some items have highly predictable next items (successor mass concentrated on few neighbours), others disperse it. A quantizer that spends its finite code resolution uniformly ignores exactly that contrast. This idea makes the behaviour contrast enter the metric tensor of the code space, so the quantizer resolves predictable regions more finely and dispersive regions more coarsely, which is where prefix transfer is already easy.
NOVELTY: Earlier attempts either weighted the assignment/outer product by transitions (Sinkhorn or behaviour-weighted assignment), set per-level or per-prefix curvature from transition statistics (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ put it in the radial coordinate, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB and Poincare-Frechet put it in the update rule). None changes the METRIC ITSELF as a function of the item's successor concentration: here the behaviour scalar is a conformal factor multiplying a fixed-curvature Lorentz distance, so the behaviour term appears inside the distance and the distance carries curvature in one expression. Curvature is held at c=1 and never estimated, respecting the gauge result (any estimated c is a radial rescale). No Frechet/Karcher codebook update, no curvature prediction from prefixes, no radial term.
CHANGE: Compute a per-item degree-corrected successor-concentration score b_i from train-only directed transitions; map it to a per-code conformal weight g_{l,k} (stop-gradient responsibility-weighted mean of g_i = exp(b_i/4)); use g_{l,k} * d_Lorentz(x_i^l, y_{l,k}) as the assignment distance at every RQ level instead of the plain distance, with the codebook update unchanged.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': '1. Train-only transitions: from the Stage-2 training split only, for each user session in timestamp order add a unit edge i -> j between consecutive distinct items; accumulate C_ij. d_i = sum_j C_ij, P_ij = C_ij / d_i.\n2. Behaviour scalar: q_i = sum_j P_ij^2 (successor concentration). Degree-matched null q_i^0 = 1/d_i. u_i = log(q_i * d_i) for d_i >= 2, else u_i = 0. b_i = clip((u_i - mean(u)) / std(u), -2, +2) over the 24556 training items (mean/std computed once on the training split, frozen).\n3. Conformal weight: g_i = exp(b_i / 4) in [e^-0.5, e^+0.5] = [0.607, 1.649].\n4. Hyperbolic lift (fixed c = 1, Lorentz chart): for tangent vector t, x = (sqrt(1+||t||^2), t), with radial clamp ||t|| <= tanh^{-1}(0.99).\n5. Code lift: y_{l,k} = (sqrt(1+||e_{l,k}||^2), e_{l,k}).\n6. Assignment logits: s_ik = - ( g_{l,k} * arccosh(-<x_i^l, y_{l,k}>_L) )^2 / tau_l, tau_l = mean_k ||e_{l,k}||^2, softmax over k, straight-through hard code for the SID.\n7. g_{l,k} = sum_i w_ik g_i / (sum_i w_ik + 1e-8), with w_ik the previous-epoch hard assignment indicator of item i to code (l,k); stop-gradient, recomputed once per epoch.\n8. Decoder input is the tangent image log_0(y_{l,k}) = e_{l,k} of the selected code (unchanged from baseline), so the generative model and Stage 3 see only integer SIDs.'}
COST: One extra O(N_items * L * K) pass per epoch for the responsibility-weighted g (24556 * 3 * 256 = 18.9M adds), plus an arccosh and a Lorentz dot replacing the squared Euclidean per pair: about 18.9M arccosh per epoch, i.e. 786k per step over 24 steps, well under 1% of a transformer step at global batch 4096; no extra parameters beyond the frozen 24556-float b vector; roughly +2-4% wall clock on Stage 2, unchanged Stage 3.
HYPOTHESIS: If the conformal stretch aligns code resolution with successor concentration, then the behaviour-weighted level-1 and level-2 quantization error should fall for high-b items at unchanged code usage, prefix transition entropy should drop for the high-b item subset, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065. It is worth keeping if that recall is above 0.065 and the behaviour-weighted quantization error falls; it is not worth keeping if g_{l,k} is nearly constant (signal washed out) or if high-b and low-b item recall move together with no prefix change.
RISKS: ['b_i may mostly encode popularity (mitigated by the degree-matched null, not guaranteed); the conformal factor may act as noise and shift code assignment without changing prefix predictability; soft responsibility may be dominated by a few hub codes so g_{l,k} collapses to 1; if high-b items are already saturated in Stage 3 the recall gain is nil; arccosh gradients blow up near the light cone if the clamp is wrong.']
END IDEA
